title: HTTP/2 specifies concurrent exchanges on the same connection
summary: HTTP/2 specifies concurrent exchanges on the same connection.
body: RFC 9113 says HTTP/2 enables a more efficient use of network resources and a reduced perception of latency by introducing header compression and allowing multiple concurrent exchanges on the same connection. The source says: "HTTP/2 enables a more efficient use of network resources and a reduced latency by introducing field compression and allowing multiple concurrent exchanges on the same connection." HTTP/2 is a mapping of HTTP semantics onto a different framing. RFC 9110 remains the semantics document. Multiplexing is a feature of the version, not a change to the meaning of a GET.
said_by: M. Thomson and C. Benfield, RFC 9113
